attrs.spatial_caveat: Two different kinds of uncertainty must not be conflated. (1) STATISTICAL CONFIDENCE - e.g. the moving block bootstrap 95% CI on the rainfall trend, or the POWER-vs-ERA5 agreement rule - says how certain we are about the value AT the queried cell itself, given measurement noise, missing data and autocorrelation. It says NOTHING about how representative that single cell is. (2) GRID-CELL REPRESENTATIVENESS - a NASA POWER value is one ~55 km model cell, ERA5 one ~11 km cell, SoilGrids and MODIS one 250 m pixel; none of them represents the whole region or a specific field, and soil texture or SOC can vary within a few meters on the ground. A trend can therefore be statistically solid (small CI) while still only describing one coarse cell - regional conclusions inherit the coarser scale, and the soil point values must be verified on farm before use.

source_disagreement.rule: POWER vs ERA5 relative difference <= 10% high, <= 25% medium, else low; downgraded one level when > 5% of the relevant POWER days are missing
